seeds.contribution: BTS survey design, filter, follow-up priority scheme, nightly volumes, per-night follow-up commitment, position definition

facts.assertion: BTS goal: spectroscopically classify all extragalactic transients brighter than 18.5 mag at peak in g or r
facts.locator: abstract; section 1 para 'The primary goal of the BTS'

facts.assertion: On a typical night in 2018 a few hundred alerts passed the BTS filter
5-15 SN candidates per night are identified by scanners and assigned for spectroscopic follow-up
SEDM priorities P3 (<18.5), P2 (18.5-18.75), P1 (>18.75); triggers active 7 d
SEDM can classify >10 SNe in the 18.5-19 mag range every night
facts.locator: section 1 para 'With the Zwicky Transient Facility'

facts.assertion: Catalog positions are the weighted average over every alert associated with the SN
761 SNe classified Apr-Dec 2018: 547 Ia, 155 II, 40 Ib/c, 19 SLSN
Filter rejects |b|<=7 deg, rbscore<0.2, known stars, moving objects, negative subtractions
Spectroscopic completeness ~96% (visual) / 93.6% to mpeak<18.5 (automated) for 2018

seeds.contribution: BTS alert volume, saved-candidate rate, quality/purity cuts, false-positive classes, class totals, redshift uncertainty, host search radius, public start date

facts.assertion: Filter reduced ~10^6 Avro alert packets per night to ~500 viable candidates (first-year filter)
facts.locator: section 2.1 para 'Our first-year in-stream software filter'

facts.assertion: 2019 filter changes cut false positives from several hundred per night to <~50
Typically 5-10 candidates saved on an average clear night
AGNs and CVs pass the filter routinely but are not part of the project; scarce spectroscopic resources reserved for genuine extragalactic transients
Public start of BTS survey 2018-06-01
SN-feature redshifts have dz~0.005 uncertainty
Host cross-match search limited to <90 arcsec and <30 kpc
facts.locator: section 2.2 para 'To provide additional counterpart photometry'

facts.assertion: 3147 classified transients in 25.5 months, 1865 pass quality+purity cuts, 1206 also m<18.5
Statistical sample 93% complete at <18.5, 97% at <18, 75% at <19
Classification success depends on season/weather (winter losses)
Classifications are the most recent TNS classification, some subtypes removed

seeds.contribution: CSV column semantics, non-completeness for Galactic/non-transient events, TNS mismatch warning, peak-mag upper-limit caveat

facts.assertion: BTS makes no attempt to be complete to Galactic events and non-transients: most are removed by the alert filter or scanners
time: time of peak expressed as JD-2458000
mag: peak P48 magnitude; if the true peak was missed this is an upper limit
Rise/Fade given as a limit when no detections deeper than 0.75 mag below peak exist
facts.locator: section 'Data Columns', items Rise and Fade

facts.assertion: TNS ID: a few transients are wrongly matched on TNS
Redshift: often approximate
LSST expects up to about ten million alerts nightly
Every SNR>5 difference-image source is a DIASource and causes an alert; every DIASource has one unique match to a DIAObject or SSObject; a new DIAObject is created when no association is possible
facts.locator: section 2.2.1 para 'All sources in a difference image'

facts.assertion: Alert packet contains the triggering DIASource, the entire DIAObject/SSObject record, and 12 months of prior DIASource/DIAForcedSource records
Alert generation in crowded fields may exceed the maximum of 10,000 alerts per visit required

seeds.contribution: alert key numbers used to derive alert-per-SN overstatement

facts.assertion: DMS supports >=10,000 alerts per standard visit on average and >=40,000 per single visit; long-term average 10^7 alerts per night assuming 1,000 visits per night
~10 million SNe in 10 years (~1 million per year); ~200 SN alerts per visit
300 observing nights per year
Alert packet <=~82 KB

seeds.contribution: DIAObject/DIASource definitions, association procedure, false-positive rate

facts.assertion: Clusters of DIASources at different times are associated with a DIAObject or SSObject to represent the underlying astrophysical phenomenon
~one background-fluctuation false positive per CCD at transSNR=5, order 200,000 per typical night
Up to ~10,000 astrophysical DIASources per visit (~10M per night)
Alert issued for each detected DIASource within 60 s; includes entire DIAObject record
Orphaned DIAObjects are deleted when their DIASources are relinked to SSObjects
Alerts issued in VOEvent format

seeds.contribution: as-built DiaObject/DiaSource tables; nDiaSources column makes alerts-per-object measurable in the PPDB

facts.assertion: DiaObject: astronomical objects detected on one or more difference images; has nDiaSources
Each diaSource is associated with either a diaObject or an ssObject

seeds.contribution: alert = one triggering diaSource + optional diaObject + history arrays

facts.assertion: Alert record keyed by diaSourceId with one diaSource, prvDiaSources array, optional diaObject

system expected to eventually produce up to seven million alerts per night
Each change triggers an alert within two minutes of image capture

about 20 billion alerts in total over the ten-year LSST

producing as many as seven million alerts of changes in the night sky each night
